question: Draft a runbook for a batch ethanol fermentation in CEN.PK113-7D on glucose, using the extracted yield records and the Yeast9 glucose ceiling as a bound.

claims.text: Yeast9 flux balance analysis gives the most ethanol obtainable from glucose by Saccharomyces cerevisiae S288C as a stoichiometric upper bound on the network, with no time axis and no vessel.
The ethanol yield on glucose recorded for wild-type CEN.PK113-7D in the overall process was measured under anaerobic fed-batch fermentation, not plain batch.

passages.quote: Table 1 Fermentation characteristics for Saccharomyces cerevisiae CEN.PK113-7D and the two mutant strains during anaerobic fed-batch fermentation at 30°C

claims.text: The ethanol yield on glucose recorded for the parental CEN.PK113-7D after ethanol adaptation was taken from a sequential-batch assay in which glucose was added after an initial aerobic growth step and the fermentation ran under anaerobic conditions.

passages.quote: After eight hours of growth at 30°C, glucose was added to the final concentration of 220 g/L to mimic the sequential-batch fermentation, and the plates were moved to an anaerobic chamber flushed with N2 gas to ensure anaerobic condition.

claims.text: The glucose-to-ethanol yield records for CEN.PK113-7D in the corpus fall below the Yeast9 glucose-to-ethanol ceiling.
No extracted record of ethanol yield on glucose for CEN.PK113-7D in a plain batch fermentation was found in the corpus.
The approved OD750 and dry cell weight SOP is the current analytics protocol that could be used to record biomass at harvest in this runbook.
The approved benchtop bioreactor CIP and sterilization SOP lists a different organism from CEN.PK113-7D, so it does not cover this strain by its own scope.

gaps: draft_runbook was refused: there is no product 'ethanol' in the catalogue. Dominion holds no ethanol molecule (a word search for ethanol returned no rows), so the runbook cannot be drafted until a person adds the product id. I did not draft a runbook and did not invent a product id.

The yield and titre records for CEN.PK113-7D are unverified candidates with no conditions field filled. The three yield records come from fed-batch and sequential-batch set-ups, so none can be bound to a plain batch run without a person checking the conditions.
No batch record binds glucose start concentration, temperature, aeration or pH for this strain. These would be needed to set the runbook's start conditions.
No kinetic fit, forecast or simulation exists in fermOS for a batch run on glucose with this strain, so no time course, end-of-run titre or hour the sugar runs out can be cited.

The Yeast9 ceiling is a generic S288C network bound computed per gram of glucose. It is not a strain-specific CEN.PK113-7D model and has no time axis, so it bounds yield but not the batch run's productivity.
No record gives biomass or dry cell weight for a plain batch run of this strain, so the OD750 and dry cell weight measure has no prediction to test.
No pureOS vessel, scale or Proforma cost run exists for this process, so a vessel design or selling price cannot be cited.

passages.heading: Materials and methods › Strains and media
passages.text: For ethanol production assays, the cells were cultivated in 24 deep-well plates containing YPD medium inoculated with overnight pre-culture to get an optical density (OD600) of 0.1. Then the yeast cells were inoculated into the YPD medium to initiate the fermentation and incubated at 30°C with shaking at 250 rpm in the aerobic phase. After eight hours of growth at 30°C, glucose was added to the final concentration of 220 g/L to mimic the sequential-batch fermentation, and the plates were moved to an anaerobic chamber flushed with N2 gas to ensure anaerobic condition. The chamber was then incubated at 30°C with shaking at 70 rpm for ethanol production. The ethanol yield was defined as the mass ratio of the ethanol titer over consumed glucose (Chang et al., 2018). All the experiments were run in triplicates, with mean and standard deviation values reported.
